insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA for probabilistic attribution; this protocol settles at ~$0.10 per verified receipt — a 50–200x cost delta driven not by efficiency gains but by structural elimination of the attribution problem itself.

With Chrome deprecating cookies and fingerprinting increasingly blocked, the industry has no cross-ecosystem, identity-free, cryptographically verified purchase signal — every current alternative (first-party data, data brokers, receipt apps) is either siloed, probabilistic, or identity-attached and therefore a regulatory liability.

Amazon knows Amazon purchases; Walmart knows Walmart purchases; neither sees the full consumer basket — the protocol's 5,328 verified receipts across grocery, dining, retail, gas, and digital commerce represent a cross-ecosystem signal that no single platform can replicate internally.

insights.topic: Category parity signal for spend allocation
insights.insight: Grocery (274 receipts, $40.84 avg basket) and restaurants/dining (265 receipts, $50.34 avg basket) are trading the top position within a few receipts of each other across consecutive 14-day windows — the stable read is near-parity in consumer frequency, not a category shift, which matters for brands allocating between CPG and foodservice.

10.6% of receipts fail standard merchant taxonomy but carry a $262.84 average basket — 6.4x the grocery average — indicating a durable B2B or high-ticket commerce segment that existing ad tech category targeting systematically misses and cannot model.

insights.topic: Digital commerce durability in verified signal
insights.insight: Amazon (9 receipts) and Shopify (7 receipts) are holding consistent positions in the 14-day brand mix alongside Walmart (76), Target (31), and Costco (30), confirming that digital-native purchase behavior is a stable component of the verified signal pool, not a single-cycle anomaly.
